follow100Note: Of the $10.67 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, non-controlling partners absorbed a $0.04 loss — $10.71 is Uber shareholders'. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Net income of $1,350M includes a $5M loss attributable to non-controlling interests; $1,355M is attributable to Uber shareholders (the $0.63 EPS figure).
oneTimers: Net income includes a $17M net headwind (pre-tax) from revaluations of Uber's equity investments; a year ago the same line contributed a $333M benefit.
otherDetail: Other income (expense), net of $162M, less $108M of interest expense and a $12M loss from equity method investments.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.note: Rides — the original Uber business. Gross Bookings rose 16% to $23.8B.

segments.name: Delivery
segments.note: Food and grocery delivery — Uber Eats and couriers. Gross Bookings rose 20% to $21.7B.

segments.name: Freight
segments.note: Trucking logistics — matching shippers with carriers. Revenue and bookings each slipped 1%.

takeaways.text: Trips grew 18% to 3.3 billion and Gross Bookings 17% to $46.8B, with Monthly Active Platform Consumers up 15%. Revenue rose 18% to $12.7B — Mobility +19%, Delivery +25%, Freight −1%.
takeaways.title: Trips kept climbing

takeaways.text: Income from operations rose to $1,450M from $796M a year ago. Adjusted EBITDA rose 35% to $2.1B — 4.5% of Gross Bookings, up from 3.9%.
takeaways.title: Operating profit nearly doubled

takeaways.text: Uber authorized a new $20B share repurchase program. Free cash flow was $2.5B in the quarter and a record $8.5B over the last twelve months.
takeaways.title: A new buyback, funded by cash flow

verdict: Uber grew revenue 18% to $12.7B as trips rose 18% to 3.3 billion, and operating profit nearly doubled to $1.5B, leaving $1.4B of profit for shareholders — plus a new $20B buyback authorization.
